other_mijikenda: Mtengedzi shared with Duruma, Giriama, Swahili (Pakia)

teaser.en: When a stomach ache is blamed on someone's evil look, this spiny bush shrub is the remedy people reach for.

summary.en: *Mtengedzi* is a spiny bush shrub with small clustered leaves and yellowish round fruits. It is used to treat *dzongo*, a stomach ailment believed to be caused by evil looks.

about.en: *Mtengedzi* is a stiff, spiny shrub of the coffee family. Its small leaves grow in clusters along the stems, often at the base of the spines. The fruits are round and yellowish when ripe.

uses.en: It is used to treat *dzongo*, a stomach ailment.

culture.en: *Dzongo* is believed to be caused by evil looks, an illness sent by a jealous or ill-wishing glance. Its second Digo name, *mdzongodzongo*, carries the name of the ailment it treats.

names.en: Pakia records two Digo names, *mtengedzi* and *mdzongodzongo*; the Mgombato dictionary also lists *mdzongodzongo* with *mtengedzi* as its equivalent. *Mtengedzi* is shared with Duruma, Giriama and Swahili. No English common name has been recorded; botanists call it *Catunaregam nilotica*.

reason.en: Another bush shrub named for the illness it treats

sources: Pakia, M. (2005) African Traditional Plant Knowledge Today: an ethnobotanical study of the Digo at the Kenya Coast. PhD thesis, Univ. Bayreuth, Appendix III (Digo–botanical name list) & Appendix VI (name semantics). https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/881/1/Pakia.pdf
